Visit dataiku.com to learn more.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
More than 800,000 people across the southeastern U.S. are without electricity
after Hurricane Isaias made landfall along the Florida panhandle last night.
Pat Duggan of Alabama Public Radio reports the storm has been downgraded to a post-tropical cyclone
but is dumping heavy rain as it makes its way north.
The National Weather Service says what's left of Isaias will make its way through Tennessee and Kentucky
as a depression after making landfall at Destin, Florida overnight.
The system is expected to drop four to eight inches of rain over the southeast with possible flash flooding
along the Gulf Coast of Alabama and Florida.
Mobile County Emergency Manager Mike Evans told residents not to rely on social media during Isaias.
I don't understand it. I know on social media with algorithms sometimes if you look at something
it could be from 12 hours ago.
Isaias broke the record setback in 1905 as the latest hurricane is formed during an Atlantic storm season.
For NPR News, I'm Pat Duggan in Tuscaloosa, Alabama.
President Trump will take his campaign swing to Tennessee today
after holding a rally in central New York last night.
NPR's Deepa Shivaram reports the president urged voters in Syracuse
to support Republican congressional candidates ahead of the November midterms.
Hello to Syracuse. We love Syracuse. Always love you.
Trump's message to New York voters was to argue that if Democrats win control of Congress, prices would go up.
He specifically focused on energy prices and his remarks in Syracuse that lasted more than 90 minutes
and wound through topics like lamenting that he did not get awarded the Nobel Peace Prize again.
Trump painted a rosy picture of the U.S. economy despite the fact that polling shows that voters disapprove
of the president's handling of it.
Trump also repeated a plea that he's been making to voters to "pretend" that he's on the ballot
in an effort to try and drum up turnout.
Deepa Shivaram, NPR News.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky says the Trump administration's decision
to lift sanctions on Russian diesel will only prolong the war.
NPR's Joanna Kekisis reports President Trump announced the deal after speaking by phone with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Trump's decision to lift sanctions on Russian diesel is the White House's latest attempt to lower fuel prices,
which have risen sharply since the U.S. war on Iran.
In a voice message to reporters, Zelensky slams Trump's decision as weak and says Russia will make billions.
"That means more money for this war, more money to inflict suffering on us," he said.
"It only feeds Putin and gives him the ability to keep fighting."
Ukraine's negotiating team is in Florida trying to restart peace talks.
Zelensky says the team is being used as "a smokescreen."
Joanna Kekisis, NPR News, Cave.
This is NPR News in Washington.
President Trump has launched a new inquiry to remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook from her position.
A White House committee says it will investigate allegations that she made false statements on mortgage applications.
Cook denies wrongdoing, and her lawyers say there's no legal basis to fire her.
The effort comes as Trump continues, pressing the central bank to lower interest rates.
A new study finds American shoppers will feel some sticker shock as they stock up on Halloween candy this year.
NPR's John Stolenest reports it's a continuing trend.
This is no trick. The average price of a 100-piece bag of assorted candy is almost $17 this year.
That's up 3.5 percent from last Halloween.
It continues. A five-year trend that has seen the cost of bags of Halloween candy increase by 71 percent, a little over $7 a bag.
The study, by FinanceBuzz, analyzed the prices of bulk Halloween sweets at four major supermarkets, Walmart, Target, Kroger, and Albertsons.
Analysts blame a rising price of cocoa due to environmental factors and supply problems in Ghana and the Ivory Coast.
Total consumer spending on Halloween is expected to reach $13.5 billion this year.
John Stolenest, NPR News.
Authorities in Italy say about 30,000 bottles of premium wine were stolen from a winery in Tuscany.
The company is warning customers to be cautious of offers outside official sales channels.
The line is worth an estimated $5.8 million. This is NPR.
